messages:
Anya: Quick proposal — let customers opt into per-route burst windows tied to a tiered SLA. idea: route-level burst = N tokens/sec for M minutes, decays to baseline. gives high-traffic routes predictable short spikes w/out messing with global pool.
Kevin: high level sounds good. need to call out billing/braking behavior. do we charge for burst separately or pull from reserved commit?
Anya: Good Q. Proposal: burst consumes a customer opt-in allowance (metered) if outside reserved pool. If within reserved pool, we mark it as "elastic-burst" and charge against headroom credits.
Jing: Implementation note: autoscale needs a cooldown tweak or we'll thrash. suggest cooldown=120s after burst-handling, and a separate prewarm path for sustained >50% for 3m.
Lina: Customers asked for per-route control (chat vs ingestion). can we expose a route label and an override in the dashboard + API?
Anya: yes — expose route_tag + consent flag. UI mock: toggle per-route "Burst Opt-in (90s)" and SLA dropdown. API: create route with body {"route":"/chat","burst_opt_in":true,"burst_window":90}.
Kevin: we should surface fallbacks in docs: what happens when burst allowance depleted — fallback to best-effort, 429s, or route-level queueing? we need default behavior.
Jing: default = best-effort degrade -> fall through to shared spot capacity -> if still starved, return 429 with Retry-After. We can also offer queued requests with max_wait param.
Lina: billing: recommend a separate line item called "route burst units" so CFOs can reconcile. also ensure free-tier customers can't opt-in without approval.
Anya: agreed. MVP scope: (1) API + route tag, (2) dashboard toggle + usage meter, (3) server runtime: enforce per-route token rate & window, (4) billing line item. Exclude queued requests and advanced prewarm for MVP.
Kevin: can we ship a thin guardrail: CLI to set global fallback behavior? e.g. `rcli capacity set-fallback --behavior=queue|best-effort|reject`
Jing: i'll prototype enforcement in runtime. pseudo-policy snippet I mocked up for review:
```
{
  "route":"/chat",
  "burst":{
    "opt_in": true,
    "window_seconds": 90,
    "tokens_per_second": 5000,
    "cooldown_seconds": 120
  },
  "fallback":"shared_spot"
}
```

Kevin: nice. add `billing_class` and `max_contiguous_spikes` fields.
Jing: added locally — will push PR with tests.
OpsBot: deploy-check: staging runtime builds passed for `burst-enforcement` branch. CI: 1/1 jobs passed.
Anya: launch criteria checklist draft: 1) API contract stable, 2) dashboard toggle visible, 3) runtime enforces window and cooldown in canary, 4) billing emits line item in test invoices, 5) docs + changelog, 6) support runbook for common customer questions.
Lina: customer ask — ACME wants 10s window with 10k tps for their ingestion route. can we support <30s windows in MVP?
Jing: technically yes but short windows complicate KPIs. suggest sticky note: allow down to 10s but require explicit ops review for >5k tps in pilot.
Anya: action items: Jing -> prototype runtime + PR by Wed; Kevin -> billing schema + line item design; Lina -> collect pilot customers & contract language; Anya -> draft launch checklist and canary plan.
Kevin: :thumbsup: add a telemetry tag `route_burst_v1` so we can measure.
Anya: agreed. final call — anyone block MVP scope?
Lina: nope, just need pilot legal ok.
Jing: no blockers from eng.
Anya: cool. I'll file RFC and add to roadmap board under Q3-ops.
OpsBot: note: scheduled canary window 2026-04-01T08:00Z.
Kevin: thanks all. we'll sync next Tue 09:30 to review PRs.
